The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages failed for shoppers
Why, in plain words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on the account page sent shoppers through a calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought nothing this month, so their account pages failed.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 12m 20s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 40.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 8,973.46 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - refuted, put back when it did not help
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #556 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages failed for shoppers
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 04:05 UTC, not back to normal by 04:17:20 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:46:07 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 04:11:28 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 11, 2026, 04:17:20 UTC - PR #556, opened as a draft

Summary
The service broke at 04:05 UTC and was not back to normal by 04:17:20 UTC, at least 12 minutes 20 seconds later. 33.8% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 40.5% failed. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by at least 8,973.46 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Switching on a new monthly spending summary on the account page sent shoppers through a calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought nothing this month, so their account pages failed. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #556, for a person to review and merge. While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, account pages could keep failing for shoppers with no purchases this month, and the same failure could come back any time the flag is switched on before the fix is in.

Impact
at least 12m 20s - since onset, still not back to normal
40.5% - peak error rate
5,268 - requests failed
1.0% to 33.8% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
at least 8,973.46 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` integer-divides the account's spend this month by the count of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. That count is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. `render_spend_summary` calls this function whenever `use_monthly_summary` is true, and the request boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns the error into a failed account page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service's share of failed requests rose far above its usual level.
  Evidence:
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 33 occurrences in 38 minutes, 03:35–04:12; # was 0.50% to 36.00%, typically 1.00%, highest at 04:06
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 15 occurrences in 8 minutes, 04:05–04:12
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
why 1 Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error first appears in the minute of the onset and does not appear before it.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 Account page requests started taking the monthly spend path. An admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at 04:05:05 UTC, and from that minute the service's per-request evaluations of the flag read on. Before that they read off, and account pages rendered normally.
  Evidence:
    P1 04:05:05 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 15 / on 185 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 04:05
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 7 occurrences in 7 minutes, 04:06–04:12
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 03:35–04:04
    Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 5 occurrences in 24 minutes, 03:39–04:02
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 04:06; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change; the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 7 hours 25 minutes before Nov 11 04:17; the Investigator Agent read back 3 production changes.
      T7
      T8
      T24
      T25
    Another flag change: the flag provider showed no flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read except this switch of monthly-spend-feature.
      T14 04:11:57 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 04:11:57
      T32 04:15:36 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 04:15:36
why 3 A reading of the source that nothing ran suggests that, with the flag on, the account page works out each shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing by the number of purchases they made this month. That would likely raise ZeroDivisionError for shoppers who have bought nothing this month. It is not settled, since the service stayed at the incident's level after the flag was switched off.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
    T18 04:14:13 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - still at the incident's level
Contributing factors
- monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for nearly all account page requests at the same moment. No staged rollout to a small share of shoppers was seen. (AI-2)
- Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for an ordinary account state such as a shopper with no purchases this month. (AI-3)
- The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 04:05:05 UTC. The newly enabled spend-summary path raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate stepped from about 1% to about 30-35%. No deployment was involved, and latency and traffic are flat. | 0.93 | refuted
C2 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at 04:05:05 UTC. Account page requests then began failing with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate rose from about 1% to about 30-35%. No deployment was involved, and latency and traffic did not move. | 0.90 | refuted, as tested for C1

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 04:12:06 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | refuted, put back when it did not help
 | 04:17:20 | Proposed a fix: PR #556 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 04:05 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 04:11:01 UTC, 6 minutes 1 second later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #556 | open
AI-2 | Turn on io-shop feature flags in stages: a small share of shoppers first, held at each stage while the account page error rate is watched, and rolled back automatically if it rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Before any io-shop feature flag can be switched on in production, require tests that run the code paths it enables with the flag on, covering ordinary account states such as a shopper with no purchases this month. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at the service that io-shop's log lines show requests evaluating the flag off, that the ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stops appearing, and that the account page error rate returns to its level before the incident. Keep it in place until the fault is fixed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Find out whether switching monthly-spend-feature off reached io-shop's per-request evaluation of the flag. Read the service's monthly-spend-feature evaluation log lines from the switch-off onward, and how src/io_shop/rollout.py turns the flag into `use_monthly_summary`, for example whether it caches the value. If requests did evaluate the flag off, find out why account page failures continued. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Before the Mitigation Agent judges a change it made, have it confirm from the service's own logs that the change reached the service. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 55 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 1 minute 5 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 6 minutes 19 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #556.
What went wrong
- When switching the flag off did not seem to help, the flag was put back on. That left on the path the logs tie to the failures, and the harm kept going.
- The second investigation came back with the same candidate as the first, which had already been tested for C1 and judged refuted. It offered nothing new to try.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault is in average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. It builds bought_this_month from the purchases flagged in_current_month and returns account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month). A shopper who has bought before but not this month has an empty list, so that line raises ZeroDivisionError. The request boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py catches that and turns it into a failed page. render_spend_summary calls this function whenever use_monthly_summary is true, so turning on monthly-spend-feature made every shopper with no purchases this month hit this line. Nothing has to be wrong with the account for that to happen: it is an ordinary state, and the shopper in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py's an_account_with_no_purchases_this_month helper, described there as "the ordinary case", is in it.

The fix: when nothing was bought this month, the function returns 0 instead of dividing. That shopper has spent nothing this month, so 0 is a true figure, not a guess covering an error. The return type stays int, so render_spend_summary and _the_figure_for / serve_account_page in src/io_shop/account_page.py take it as they take any other figure. Nothing is caught or silenced. The empty case is checked before dividing, and any other failure still reaches the boundary as before. The lifetime function average_spend_per_item is unchanged and still raises for an account with no purchases at all. Its line number is unchanged too, so tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py's check that the reported line holds // still points at it.

Tests added to tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py:
• One calls average_spend_per_item_this_month on a shopper with no purchases this month and asserts 0. With the current code that call raises ZeroDivisionError.
• One calls render_spend_summary with use_monthly_summary=True for the same shopper and asserts 0.

Not settled here: the investigation's open question of why errors continued after the flag was switched off. This patch does not explain or address it. The code I read only shows the monthly path being chosen when the caller passes use_monthly_summary=True. I did not read how that boolean is evaluated (e.g. src/io_shop/rollout.py).
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

✗ Root-cause analysis complete (not met)

○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, account pages failed for some shoppers for {duration}. The trouble began when a new monthly spending summary was switched on for the account page. The summary sends shoppers through a calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought nothing this month, so it was likely those shoppers whose account pages failed. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one, so it cost the responders no call-outs. Argus switched the new feature back off, but that did not help, so Argus switched it on again. Argus then proposed a fix, which is open as a draft. It has not been put in place yet.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
